extracted.intended_audience: parties to Investigation No. 337-TA-1365, interested government agencies, and other interested persons (e.g., counsel, industry stakeholders, importers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for filing written submissions to the U.S. International Trade Commission in Investigation No. 337-TA-1365 addressing issues under review and the topics of remedy, the public interest, and bonding. Includes deadlines, page limits, required content, confidentiality procedures, and filing format guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues under Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has determined to review the FID's: (1) construction of the “aperture” terms recited in the asserted claims of the '153 Patent; (2) finding that the accused products infringe the asserted claims of the '153 patent; (3) finding that the asserted claims of the '153 patent are not invalid under 35 U.S.C. 112 for lack of written description and/or indefiniteness; and (4) finding that Shoals' domestic industry products satisfy the domestic industry requirement of section 337, including the FID's findings concerning the technical prong and the economic prong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are invited to brief only the discrete issues requested above. The parties are not to brief other issues on review, which are adequately presented in the parties' existing filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific record-identification questions for parties
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Please identify whether and where in the record Shoals presented arguments with supporting evidence that the accused products infringe any asserted claim of the '153 patent under OUII's proposed construction of the “aperture” terms. (2) Please identify whether and where in the record Shoals presented arguments with supporting evidence that its domestic industry products satisfy the technical prong of the domestic industry requirement of section 337 under OUII's proposed construction of the “aperture” terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parties are invited to brief only these discrete issues requested above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of remedy to address
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute authorizes issuance of, inter alia, (1) an exclusion order that could result in the exclusion of the subject articles from entry into the United States; and/or (2) cease and desist orders that could result in the respondents being required to cease and desist from engaging in unfair acts in the importation and sale of such articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is interested in receiving written submissions that address the form of remedy, if any, that should be ordered. If a party seeks exclusion of an article from entry into the United States for purposes other than entry for consumption, the party should so indicate and provide information establishing that activities involving other types of entry either are adversely affecting it or likely to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant obligations in initial submission re remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: In its initial submission, Complainant is also requested to identify the remedy sought and Complainant and OUII are requested to submit proposed remedial orders for the Commission's consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant is further requested to state the dates that the Asserted Patents expire, to provide the HTSUS subheadings under which the accused products are imported, and to supply the identification information for all known importers of the products at issue in this investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest factors to address
rubrics_metrics.description: The public interest factors the Commission will consider include the effect that an exclusion order and cease and desist orders would have on: (1) the public health and welfare, (2) competitive conditions in the U.S. economy, (3) U.S. production of articles that are like or directly competitive with those that are subject to investigation, and (4) U.S. consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is therefore interested in receiving written submissions that address the aforementioned public interest factors in the context of this investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonding submissions and Presidential Review period effect
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 60-day period of Presidential Review, the subject articles would be entitled to enter the United States under bond, in an amount determined by the Commission and prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is therefore interested in receiving submissions concerning the amount of the bond that should be imposed if a remedy is ordered. (The RD recommended a bond of 100 percent during the period of Presidential Review.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to the investigation, interested government agencies, and any other interested parties are encouraged to file written submissions on the issues of remedy, the public interest, and bonding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and page limits for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial written submissions must be filed no later than close of business on November 27, 2024. Reply submissions must be filed no later than the close of business on December 5, 2024. Opening submissions are limited to 50 pages. Reply submissions are limited to 25 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further submissions on these issues will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing procedures and cover page requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons filing written submissions must file the original document electronically on or before the deadlines stated above. The Commission's paper filing requirements in 19 CFR 210.4(f) are currently waived. Submissions should refer to the investigation number (“Inv. No. 337-TA-1365”) in a prominent place on the cover page and/or the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures (https://www.usitc.gov/documents/handbook_on_filing_procedures.pdf). Persons with questions regarding filing should contact the Secretary, (202) 205-2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential-submission marking and redaction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to submit a document to the Commission in confidence must request confidential treatment by marking each document with a header indicating that the document contains confidential information. This marking will be deemed to satisfy the request procedure set forth in Rules 201.6(b) and 210.5(e)(2) (19 CFR 201.6(b) & 210.5(e)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents for which confidential treatment by the Commission is properly sought will be treated accordingly. Any non-party wishing to submit comments containing confidential information must serve those comments on the parties to the investigation pursuant to the applicable Administrative Protective Order. A redacted non-confidential version of the document must also be filed with the Commission and served on any parties to the investigation within two business days of any confidential filing. All nonconfidential written submissions will be available for public inspection on EDIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and use of submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: All information, including confidential business information and documents for which confidential treatment is properly sought, submitted to the Commission for purposes of this investigation may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing or maintaining the records of this or a related proceeding, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations relating to the programs, personnel, and operations of the Commission including under 5 U.S.C. appendix 3; or (ii) by U.S. Government employees and contract personnel, solely for cybersecurity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contract personnel will sign appropriate nondisclosure agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation on briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties are invited to brief only the discrete issues requested above. The parties are not to brief other issues on review, which are adequately presented in the parties' existing filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs outside the discrete requested issues are not to be filed unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of non-confidential record and docket access
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of non-confidential documents filed in connection with this investigation may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov. All nonconfidential written submissions will be available for public inspection on EDIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For help accessing EDIS, email EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of target date extension and Commission authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has determined to extend the target date for this investigation to January 15, 2025. The authority for the Commission's determination is contained in section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1337), and in part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR part 210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's vote on this determination took place on November 13, 2024.
